goldens.comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:245 — Federated rules are now treated as mutable because the wrapper discarded the group-level federated check and hard-codes `isFederated` false.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in useAllRulerRuleAbilities (lines 243-275), the code now hard-codes `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO comment saying 'Add support for federated rules'. Previously in useAllAlertRuleAbilities, there was a call to `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` that properly checked if a rule group was federated. Federated rule groups should be treated as immutable (not editable/removable), but with this change they will be treated as mutable since isFederated is always false. This is a real correctness bug where federated rules could incorrectly appear editable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165 — Prometheus-only Grafana list rows can never show Delete because the render guard still requires the ruler rule that the new loader no longer supplies.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that Delete cannot be shown for Prometheus-only Grafana list rows because the render guard requires the ruler rule. However, examining the diff in AlertRuleMenu.tsx, the component now uses BOTH useRulerRuleAbilities (for rulerRule) AND useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities (for promRule). The canDelete logic at line 89-90 shows: `const canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`. This means if rulerRule is undefined but promRule is a valid Grafana rule, the grafana abilities will be checked and can return true for delete permission. The component is specifically designed to handle the case where only promRule is available, which is the stated purpose in the comment at lines 38-41.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104 — Clicking Silence on a Prometheus-only Grafana row is a no-op because the drawer render condition still requires the absent ruler rule.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is rendered with condition `{SilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} onClose={() => setSilenceDrawer(false)} />}`. The `rule` prop here is `RulerRuleDTO | undefined`. When only promRule is provided (no rulerRule), `rule` is undefined, but the drawer still attempts to render with `rulerRule={rule}` which would be undefined. The SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer component likely requires a valid rulerRule to function. This means clicking Silence when only promRule exists (Prometheus-only Grafana row) would either crash or be a no-op since the drawer receives undefined for rulerRule.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123 — Prometheus-only Grafana list rows can never show Pause because the menu still requires an absent ruler rule even when the new Prometheus ability grants it.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that Prometheus-only Grafana list rows can never show Pause because the menu requires an absent ruler rule. However, looking at the diff in AlertRuleMenu.tsx lines 53-99, the code now checks BOTH rulerRule abilities AND grafanaPromRule abilities using OR logic: `canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)`. This means if rulerRule is undefined/absent, the grafanaPauseAbility from useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities can still grant the Pause permission. The code explicitly handles the case where only promRule exists by using the grafana abilities as a fallback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:324 — Grafana recording rules lose their Export action because the Prometheus ability supports ModifyExport only for alerting rules whereas the replaced ruler ability supported every Grafana-managed rule.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in useAbilities.ts, the new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` function at line 324 sets `[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` where `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. This means recording rules (where isAlertingRule is false) will have ModifyExport support set to false. In contrast, the original `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` function at line 263 uses `[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, exportAllowed]` where `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which returns true for any Grafana-managed rule (both alerting and recording). This is a behavioral regression where Grafana recording rules lose their Export capability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:287 — Duplicating the full action-policy and editability logic for a second DTO forces future permission changes to be maintained in two paths.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (lines 285-340) which duplicates much of the logic from `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (lines 232-275), including permission checking, provisioned/federated/plugin-provided rule detection, and ability mapping. Both functions have similar structures for determining canPause, canDelete, canDuplicate, etc. This is a legitimate architectural concern - if permission policies change, both functions need to be updated in sync. The finding correctly identifies this duplication at line 287 where the new function begins implementing parallel logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:287 — The new Prom-rule ability engine has no direct tests for provisioned, recording, plugin-provided, loading, missing-folder, or skip-token branches, so permission regressions can ship unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` hook (lines 287-340) with complex branching logic for provisioned rules, recording rules, plugin-provided rules, loading states, and folder permissions. Looking at the test file changes (GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx), the tests focus on UI interactions (More button, menu items, permissions for edit/delete) but don't directly unit test the new ability hook's branches. The finding correctly identifies that the new permission engine in useAbilities.ts lacks direct unit tests for its various code paths (isProvisioned, isPluginProvided, loading state, missing folder via useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable). While some integration testing exists through the component tests, the complex permission logic in the new hook could regress without dedicated unit tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rules/RulesTable.test.tsx:68 — RBAC coverage mocks the new ability hooks themselves instead of exercising their real permission computation, so these tests can stay green when production authorization behavior is wrong.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test file mocks the new ability hooks (useRulerRuleAbilities, useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities) directly rather than testing their actual implementation. Looking at the diff in RulesTable.test.tsx, lines 57-75 show mocks being set up for all the ability hooks, and throughout the tests these mocks return hardcoded values. This is a valid architectural concern - the tests verify UI behavior given certain permissions but don't verify that the permission computation logic in the actual hooks works correctly. However, this is a testing strategy choice rather than a bug, and unit tests for hooks would typically be separate from component tests. The finding is specific and grounded in the diff.
